newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper seen lower, aluminium to firm.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper seen lower, aluminium to firm.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Rising stocks, contracting nearby backwardations and downtrending chart signals are likely to see copper adopt a downside bias, traders and chartists said on Thursday.
By contrast, aluminium looked likely to firm further and test initial resistance at $1,650 a tonne and then $1,675 amid falling inventories and physical tightness, they added.
COPPER - With London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks above 200,000 tonnes and expected to rise further over the coming days, traders and analysts expected copper prices to come under downside pressure.

Narrowing in nearby spreads and downtrending chart signals were likely to further dent sentiment and several market operators were expecting a test of resistance at $2,240 a tonne in the near term. "Higher stocks and seasonal weakness make copper an opportunist sell at present," brokers GNI said in their daily commodity report.
According to LME brokers Brandeis, a failure to move above resistance at $2,306 was likely to see crucial support at the $2,250 level coming under examination.
Others were looking for copper to fall towards $2,240 with a breach of that level likely to see a retracement to $2,226.
In early trading copper's cash to three months backwardation was indicated at $58/$63, compared with $60/$65 on Wednesday and a peak of $270 last week.
Several traders expected the backwardation to ease further.
On the upside resistance at $2,340 needed to be overcome, but they doubted whether that would be tested this week.
"All in all copper has little going for it on the upside," one LME floor trader commented.
At 0718 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,272/76, against Wednesday's London close of $2,276/78.

ALUMINIUM - A move towards $1,675 was expected in the near term, but the market might encounter some resistance around $1,650. "With the strong close (Wednesday) and the technical indicators extending towards the highs we are looking for further challenges of overhead resistance," Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said.
LME stocks were expected to fall on Thursday, while nearby spreads are expected to remain tight.
Support was likely to emerge at $1,600.
Harry Creates of Amalgamated Metal Trading noted a downside gap to fill between $1,627 and $1,620.
At 0818 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,639/41, versus $1,641/43.
